synopsis: The booklet treats FMI as a major generic simulation-tool integration mechanism and rates FMI/SSP as domain-neutral and transferable to off-road work [f8712, f7167, f13224]. FMI co-simulation can connect reduced-order in-house models with commercial high-fidelity components; Simulink–Mevea integration over FMI or TCP/IP is explicitly supported [f6395, f8699]. By mid-2025, the Modelica Association reported around 250 FMI-supporting tools, with extensive co-simulation support [f8713, f15863]. Recommendations call for OSI and FMI/SSP interfaces with adapters to simulation, HIL and physical automation, and for simulation-tool RFPs to require open-format export including FMI [f7203, f16487]. Adoption does not eliminate integration work: FMI-linked components are rated medium effort because semantics still require calibration, while Chapter 9 explicitly says the research did not verify FMI/SSP's status [f8729, f7165].
